body:
> I don't think `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE` will emit on a script when performing C# rebuild (aka ALC reloading).

That's correct, because the resource is not being _deleted_, only the script instance. When the C# project is rebuilt, all C# scripts are disposed and recreated, but the native objects they were attached to aren't affected.

> The issue has been resolved after modifying your code to use the event functions from the ISerialization Listener.

I would advise against using `ISerializationListener`, it's an internal interface not meant for user consumption[^1]. Although it may be needed in some scenarios, I don't think it's the case here. If all you need to do is cleanup you can override the `Dispose` method, but I don't think that's what we want here either.

For this scenario, the compositor effect creates new mesh instances using the `RenderingServer` APIs. We likely don't want to destroy and recreate these instances when rebuilding the C# project since, as mentioned earlier, the native objects persist across assembly reloads.

You are currently using the constructor to initialize the compositor effect and create the meshes (as recommended by Godot's [compositor documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/compositor.html)). However, we need to call the C# constructor when recreating the C# instance, so the initialization code will be executed again when reloading the assembly. Moving this initialization to `ISerializationListener.OnAfterDeserialize` is not really the solution, you are still initializing the compositor effect multiple times, recreating it when the assembly is reloaded.

A better approach would be to have some `_isInitialized` flag that you can set to `true` in your `_InitializeCompute` method. Then, you can check at the beginning of that method to see if the compositor effect is already initialized.

The issue you will find with this approach is that the state will not be preserved across reloads. The `_isInitialized` flag as well as the other fields will reset to the default value. This is because Godot doesn't know anything about these fields, since they are not exported. If you export them they should be preserved across reloads, but the state is restored after calling the constructor and, since you are calling the `_InitializeCompute` method in the constructor, it may be too late.

We keep getting reports about C# tool scripts and reloading assemblies, which makes me think we need to rethink how the reloading process works. This is one of the reasons I don't want users using the `ISerializationListener` interface, since when we change the reloading process we'll likely break that API.

[^1]: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/issues/10615#issuecomment-2635063398

> I would advise against using ISerializationListener, it's an internal interface not meant for user consumption

Oh, I wasn't aware of that. Thanks for mentioning it. I have put up a [proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11819) about the unloading usability issue recently; it would be great if we could restructure the mono module to a point where there is no need for users to know about unloading at all.
